messages:
Sara (Support): Hey team — escalation from ACME: their rerank calls to /v1/rerank are intermittently returning 400 'invalid candidates schema' and when they do get scores the numbers look way off (very negative). They pasted the payload, see below. Customer says this started after they switched from an internal reranker to Redwood. They also complained latency spiked (~2.5s p95).
Maria (CS): Thanks, Sara. Can you paste the exact request body and the client library + version? Also any request id from the server logs would help.
Sara (Support): Here's the sanitized payload they sent (they're sending nested docs -> passages -> candidates):
```
{
  "query": { "text": "find company updates about Q3" },
  "documents": [
    { "id": "doc1", "passages": [ { "text": "Q3 earnings released..." }, { "text": "product roadmap Q3..." } ] },
    { "id": "doc2", "passages": [ { "text": "press release: new hire" } ] }
  ]
}
```
Sara (Support): They expected the service to handle nested documents and return a per-document rerank score. Instead they get a 400 sometimes, and when it succeeds the scores are per-passage and not aggregated.
Ryan (Platform): I pulled the request id they sent (rq_01Fb...) — logs show our parser rejected payloads that don't include a top-level `candidates` array of strings/objects. The error path is `validation.candidates.missing`. The backend currently accepts either `candidates` (preferred) or `documents` only if it's the old compatibility flag, but we don't auto-flatten `documents.passages` -> `candidates` unless the compatibility flag is set. Seems their client/library toggled that flag off.
Aditya (ML): That also explains scoring. Our reranker model scores each candidate string. If you pass passages as separate candidates, the scores are per-passage. We previously had logic to aggregate passage scores up to doc-level (max/avg), but that path is only triggered when the request explicitly sets `candidate_granularity: "document"` or uses the older `documents` shape. If they flatten server-side unexpectedly, the semantics change.
Maria (CS): Customer thought `query` could be an object (they sent `{ "text": "..." }`) — our docs show `query` as a string in examples. Does the parser accept both? They also mentioned seeing a 413 for large payloads.
Ryan (Platform): We accept `query` as either a string or object `{text: string, language?: string}`; we coerce to string by taking `text`. But the validator branch for nested documents expects `query` to be a string, so if you send the object we sometimes hit a schema mismatch in the older compatibility path. 413s are from max payload size (1MB) — they sent ~1.2MB because of many long passages.
Sara (Support): Customer is blocked — they want a clear repro and a workaround to send ASAP.
Aditya (ML): Short-term fix for them: flatten passages client-side into `candidates` with objects like `{ "id": "doc1_p1", "text": "Q3 earnings released...", "meta": {"doc_id": "doc1"} }` and send `candidate_granularity: "passage"`. If they want doc-level scores, set `aggregate: "avg_by_doc"` and we will post-process by grouping on `meta.doc_id`.
Ryan (Platform): I can also add a compatibility shim to accept `documents` with nested `passages` and auto-flatten into `candidates` for a few weeks while we update docs. That will reduce 400s. Will push a small change but need CS signoff since semantics change.
Maria (CS): Please also capture the exact error messages from the API and return better guidance (e.g., "expected top-level candidates array or set compatibility=true to accept nested documents"). Right now the 400 only says `invalid candidates schema` which is unhelpful.
DeployBot: ✅ PR #4127 merged to staging: accept `documents` with `passages` as alias for `candidates` when `compatibility_mode=true`. Rolling out to canary cluster.
Ryan (Platform): Deployed to canary. Sara, can you ask ACME to retry against the canary endpoint (same host with `-canary` suffix)? If they still see bad scores, include `x-rerank-request-id` from the response headers.
Sara (Support): Sent canary URL + quick client-side flatten example to ACME. Also asked them to switch `query` to plain string to avoid hitting old validator branch. Waiting on repro.
(15m later)
ACME via email: Tried canary -> 200 OK. Scores look reasonable now when we flattened passages. But they reported higher billable token counts — they were surprised by cost when flattening.
Maria (CS): Explain cost: each passage becomes a candidate and is scored; more candidates -> more model forward passes (roughly linear cost). Offer to run a quick eval on a sample set and suggest `candidate_threshold` to limit num candidates per query.
Aditya (ML): For follow-up: we should add a rerank setting `max_candidates_per_doc` and a `dedupe_passages` heuristic. Also doc change: clarify `query` field format (string preferred), show both minimal and nested examples, and document aggregation strategies (`max`, `avg`, `avg_by_doc`) with examples.
Ryan (Platform): I'll open infra ticket to increase payload 1MB -> 5MB for enterprise plans and to add clearer 400 messages. Also will add a log annotation so CS can see whether we auto-flattened.
Maria (CS): Action items:
- Sara: confirm ACME is unblocked and collect their sample payloads + sample scores (due EOD).
- Ryan: infra PR to improve errors + canary rollout to prod if canary is green (ETA 24h).
- Aditya: doc PR with aggregation examples + recommended client-side pattern (flatten + meta) (ETA 2 days).
- Product: consider product-level `compatibility_mode` opt-in table and pricing note for candidate-heavy usage.
Sara (Support): Acknowledged. I'll attach ACME's sanitized sample and close the escalation once they confirm stable.
Ryan (Platform): Noted. I'll post a short internal note in #eng-runtime summarizing root cause — mismatched schema + implicit flattening changed scoring semantics. Will also add a monitoring alert for sudden increases in candidate count per request.
Maria (CS): Thanks team. Can we also update the quickstart examples to show the minimal valid payload to avoid similar confusion? Example to include:
```
POST /v1/rerank
{
  "query": "find company updates about Q3",
  "candidates": [
    "Q3 earnings released...",
    "product roadmap Q3..."
  ],
  "aggregate": "avg"
}
```
Aditya (ML): One last note — if customers want to pass structured query metadata, send `query_text` + `query_meta` instead of wrapping in an object; we'll accept both but docs should be explicit.
Sara (Support): ACME confirmed stable after flattening and canary. Closing escalation once deploy to prod is live. :thumbsup:
